When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Linear

## discord-setup
Discord Server Setup MCP Server

This server provides tools for automating Discord server setup using the Discord Bot API.
It can discover servers, create/manage channels, create/manage roles, configure settings, and apply templates.

Available tool categories:
- Guild: List servers, select active server, get server info
- Channels: Create/edit/delete channels and categories
- Roles: Create/edit/delete/list/reorder roles
- Settings: Configure server verification, content filter, notifications
- Templates: Apply pre-built server templates (gaming, community, business, study-group)

Role hierarchy note: Discord positions are inverted — a HIGHER position number is
higher/more powerful, @everyone is position 0 at the bottom, and newly created
roles default to the bottom. Use list_roles to see the current order, create_role
with placement:"top"/"above"/"below" to rank a role, and reorder_roles with a
top-first orderedRoleIds list rather than hand-computing position numbers.

Prerequisites:
- Discord bot created at https://discord.com/developers/applications
- Bot token configured via DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN environment variable or ~/.discord-mcp/config.json
- Bot invited to Discord server(s) with appropriate permissions (Manage Server, Manage Roles, Manage Channels)

Setup Instructions:
1. Create a Discord application at https://discord.com/developers/applications
2. Add a bot user and copy the bot token
3. Set DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN environment variable or create ~/.discord-mcp/config.json with your token
4. Generate OAuth2 URL with bot scope and required permissions
5. Invite bot to your Discord server(s)

Workflow:
1. Use list_guilds to see available servers
2. Use select_guild to set the active server
3. Use other tools to manage channels, roles, etc.

 - **Apply setup** changes the run's loadout to a setup from your library and hands it out to the tool, set in its settings. The list is your library for the pack's tool; a tool has to be attached to the run for the hand-out to reach it.
 - **Command** sends a setup's operations to the tool once, without changing the run's own setup. A warp is the usual one: it moves the player without swapping what the run is holding them to.
 - **Undo** takes back the last result. It is lit when there is something to take back and dim when there is not.

## Review: task 33 — `feat(deck): a profile built from the run it is on, handed to the stream deck app` (4a4f8b9)

Worktree clean, only commit on `a-profile-from-the-run` off `c1d695e`. No unstaged `packages/cli/src/bin.ts` was present.

### Spec compliance

**Package (`packages/deck-profiles`)**

- ✅ `Keyed` exactly as the brief specifies: `packages/deck-profiles/src/profiles.ts:154-162` — `moves`/`counters`/`resources` id-only, `setups`/`commands` `{id,title}`. Exported from `src/index.ts:17,24,31-32`.
- ✅ `fromPack(pack, setups)` at `profiles.ts:189-199`, `fromOffer(offer)` at `profiles.ts:214-224`. `fromOffer` classifies by title over `commands` (`isWarp`), then partitions `setups` by the resulting warp-id set, so each setup gets exactly one key — the accepted ruling.
- ✅ Premise of the ruling verified independently: `apps/web/src/run/RunView.tsx:459,465` builds `setups: offeredSetups` and `commands: offeredSetups.filter(fitsTheWire)`, so `commands ⊆ setups` and taking `commands` at face value would double-key most setups.
- ✅ `packKeys` now takes `Keyed` only (`profiles.ts:240-253`); the setup/command keys are laid down as one run sorted by `title.localeCompare` (`profiles.ts:251`) — the interleave ruling.
- ✅ Interleave does not change the other caller: `apps/web/src/library/DeckProfiles.tsx:74` feeds `forTool(await setupsHere(), tool)`, and `setupsHere` already sorts by `title.localeCompare` (`apps/web/src/control/setups.ts:61`). Same order, so the Marketplace download is unchanged too.
- ✅ 44 zips byte-identical. `npx vitest run packages/deck-profiles -t "byte for byte"` passes; the test asserts `expect(all).toHaveLength(44)` and a `Buffer.equals` against each committed file (`profiles.test.ts:348-356`). No `.streamDeckProfile` appears in the diffstat.
- ✅ `specs(pack|null, setups, device?)` keeps its exact signature as a one-line wrapper over `specsFor` (`profiles.ts:385-387`); `design/profiles.mjs` and `DeckProfiles.tsx` are untouched.
- ✅ Adapter-equivalence test: `profiles.test.ts:283-325` builds a real-shaped offer (moves, both tracker kinds, setups, commands) from the demo pack plus one plain setup and one warp, and asserts `packKeys(fromOffer(offer))` equals `packKeys(fromPack(demo, setups))` **and** the built container bytes match. A second test (`:327-339`) pins the one-key-per-setup rule.
- ✅ No Node built-ins in production code: `grep -rn "node:" packages/deck-profiles/src` excluding tests returns only a prose mention in `sha1.ts:6`. `layouts.ts` dropped its `@runlog/rules-schema` import (`isWarp` now takes `{title, ops?}` at `layouts.ts:119-121`); `profiles.ts:1` keeps a `import type` only, which is fine.

**Plugin (`streamdeck/src/profiles-on-demand.ts`)**

- ✅ `buildFor(state, device)` returns `{file, bytes}` or `null` for no snapshot, no `packId`, or a deck with no grid (`profiles-on-demand.ts:53-56`). Tested for all three (`profiles-on-demand.test.ts:106-116`, Pedal type 5 → null).
- ✅ Slug is file-safe. `slugFor` (`profiles-on-demand.ts:41-43`) = `replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]+/g,"-").replace(/^[-.]+/,"") || "pack"`. I probed it directly: `"../x"→"x"`, `"a/b"→"a-b"`, `"..\\..\\win"→"win"`, `"..."→"pack"`, `""→"pack"`, `"C:/abs/path"→"C-abs-path"`, `"\0x"→"x"`. No separator, no drive colon, no leading `..` survives. The `-${deck}` suffix also means a `con`/`nul` pack id cannot produce a Windows reserved filename.
- ✅ Written to `join(cwd(), "profiles", "on-demand")` with `mkdirSync(…, {recursive:true})` (`profiles-on-demand.ts:59-63`). The SDK resolution claim checks out: `node_modules/@elgato/streamdeck/dist/plugin/logging/index.js:8` is `dest: path.join(cwd(), "logs")` — same base.
- ✅ `install(file)` = `streamDeck.system.openUrl(pathToFileURL(file).href)` (`profiles-on-demand.ts:71`).
- ✅ One log line per build (`:64`) and one per hand-over (`:72`), carrying only the slug and deck name. Test asserts `mock.logged` has length exactly 2 (`profiles-on-demand.test.ts:470`). Nothing secret.

**First attach (`streamdeck/src/plugin.ts:78-97`)**

- ✅ Gated on the generic fallback: `PACK_PROFILES[packId] === undefined`, which is exactly the condition under which `profileFor` falls back to `GENERIC_PROFILE` (`streamdeck/src/profiles.ts:41-45`).
- ✅ Gated on the setting: the guard is `if (!switchProfiles …) return`, and `switchProfiles = g.switchProfiles !== false` (`plugin.ts:140`), so unset is on and only an explicit `false` turns it off.
- ✅ Once per pack id per plugin run: module-level `const offered = new Set<string>()` (`plugin.ts:74`), added before the device loop.
- ✅ The existing switch still happens — the build sits inside the loop before `switchToProfile`, and the pre-existing test "puts a run of a pack it ships no layout for on the generic profile" (`plugin.test.ts:147-156`) still passes with an unshipped pack.
- ✅ Tested: builds once then not again for the same pack (`plugin.test.ts:174-190`), nothing for a shipped pack while the switch still fires (`:192-202`), nothing with the setting off (`:204-212`).

**Open key**

- ✅ Target `profile` builds and hands over (`streamdeck/src/actions/open.ts:27-36`), alerting when `buildFor` returns null.
- ✅ Gated like `run`: `openFace` falls through `common(state)` before answering `profile` (`state.ts:392-394`); label "This pack's profile" (`state.ts:378`), `when: "to import"`. Tested at `state.test.ts:685-692` for signed-out and no-run-picked.
- ✅ `ui/open.html:18` lists `<option value="profile">This pack's profile</option>`.
- ✅ Tested with `openUrl` and `node:fs` mocked: `open.test.ts:138-148` asserts one write, one `file:///…` URL containing `demo-xl.streamDeckProfile`, plus an alert case with no snapshot.

**Docs**

- ✅ Guide profiles paragraph rewritten (`apps/web/src/guide/pages/stream-deck.mdx:5`) and the Open key bullet gained the new setting (`:39`). `streamdeck/README.md:20,24`.
- ✅ No em dashes or en dashes anywhere in the added lines (grep over `^+` for U+2013/U+2014: none).
- ✅ American English (grep for colour/behaviour/licence/organis/customis/centre/recognise/analyse/catalogue in added lines: none).
- ✅ No packs named in any doc copy at all. Test fixtures use invented `com.example.*` ids; nothing touches the private pack.

**Manifest and checks**

- ✅ `git diff c1d695e..4a4f8b9 -- …/manifest.json` is empty; the only file changed under `com.scrthq.runlog.sdPlugin/` is `ui/open.html`. The new Open target needs nothing in the manifest (the target lives in the property inspector).
- ✅ `npx --workspace streamdeck streamdeck validate com.scrthq.runlog.sdPlugin` → "Validation successful".
- ✅ Commit subject is exactly `feat(deck): a profile built from the run it is on, handed to the stream deck app`, empty body, no trailers.

**Commands run**

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `npx vitest run packages/deck-profiles streamdeck apps/web/src/guide --no-file-parallelism` | 26 files, 253 tests, all pass |
| byte-identical zip test alone | pass (44 asserted) |
| `npm run typecheck` | clean |
| `npm run lint:docs` | 0 issues |
| `npm run format:check` | clean |
| `npm run build -w streamdeck` | built; only the pre-existing circular-dependency and TS5096 warnings |
| `streamdeck validate` | successful |
| `git status --porcelain` after all of it | clean |

### Strengths

- The `Keyed` seam is the right cut. One layout function, two adapters, and the equivalence test holds the adapters against each other rather than against a snapshot, so the day the offer and the pack file disagree the test says so.
- The interleave decision is backed by evidence rather than asserted: the 44-zip byte test would have caught a setups-then-commands order, and the web caller's sort was already `title.localeCompare`, so both existing callers keep their exact output.
- `slugFor` is genuinely safe, not just safe-looking: no separator on either platform survives it, no leading `..`, and the mandatory `-<deck>` suffix rules out Windows reserved device names as a side effect.
- `buildFor` is a pure-ish function returning bytes as well as a path, so the Open key test can assert on the URL and the package test on the layout without either reaching a real disk.
- The `fromOffer` docblock and the report both record the warp-classification gap rather than papering over it.

### Issues

**Critical** — none.

**Important**

1. `streamdeck/.gitignore` does not cover the new runtime output. It already carries `*.sdPlugin/bin` and `*.sdPlugin/logs`, which exist precisely because `npm run watch` links the repo's `.sdPlugin` folder into the Stream Deck app and the SDK writes into it at `cwd()`. `buildFor` writes to the same base, so a dev session that follows a run of an unshipped pack leaves `streamdeck/com.scrthq.runlog.sdPlugin/profiles/on-demand/<packid>-<deck>.streamDeckProfile` untracked in the repo, named after the pack id. Given the private-pack boundary, a stray `git add -A` is a plausible way for that id to land in a commit. One line fixes it: `*.sdPlugin/profiles/on-demand` beside the other two. (CI packs from a clean checkout, so the release artifact is not at risk.)

**Minor**

2. `offered.add(packId)` happens before the device loop (`plugin.ts:86`), so if `streamDeck.devices` is empty or holds only Pedals at that moment, the pack is marked as offered and never built for the rest of the plugin run — a deck plugged in later gets nothing. The pre-existing `switchedFor` gate has the same shape, so this is consistent rather than new, but the two flags now guard different things.
3. `buildFor` does not check `hasKeys`. A run whose pack publishes no moves, counters or resources still writes a file and raises an import prompt for what amounts to the generic layout plus a Rules key. The brief scoped the null cases to "no snapshot, no device layout", so this is in spec; the package already exports `hasKeys` and the web page uses it to decide whether to offer a download at all, so the two surfaces now differ on that question.
4. The adapter equivalence holds only where `commands == setups`. A warp that `fitsTheWire` rejects appears in `setups` but not `commands`, so `fromOffer` gives it an Apply setup key while `fromPack` would give it a Command key. This is arguably the correct answer (the page offers no Command for it either), but it is a second divergence beside the documented op-only-warp one and is neither commented nor tested.
5. Nothing ties `ui/open.html`'s option list to the `OpenTarget` union, so a seventh target could be added in one place and not the other. Pre-existing gap, not introduced here.
6. `install` is called once per device on first attach, so a two-deck desk gets two import prompts at once — the accepted ruling, noted here only because the guide copy says "the Stream Deck app asks whether to import it", singular, and a two-deck streamer will see two.

### Assessment

**Task quality: Approved**

The commit does what the brief asked and the parts that were most likely to go wrong are the parts held down hardest: the 44 committed zips rebuild byte for byte, the two adapters are tested against each other rather than against a golden file, the slug sanitizer survives every traversal shape I threw at it, and the plugin-dir resolution matches the SDK's own `join(cwd(), "logs")` line rather than guessing. Every command in the brief runs clean, the manifest is untouched, the docs name no packs and carry no em dashes, and the commit subject and trailer-free body are exact. The one thing worth fixing before merge is the missing `.gitignore` entry for `profiles/on-demand`, which is a one-line change with a real private-pack leak path behind it; the rest are notes for the next pass rather than blockers.

| `npm run build -w streamdeck` | built; only the pre-existing circular-dependency and TS5096 warnings |
| `streamdeck validate` | successful |
| `git status --porcelain` after all of it | clean |

### Strengths

- The `Keyed` seam is the right cut. One layout function, two adapters, and the equivalence test holds the adapters against each other rather than against a snapshot, so the day the offer and the pack file disagree the test says so.
- The interleave decision is backed by evidence rather than asserted: the 44-zip byte test would have caught a setups-then-commands order, and the web caller's sort was already `title.localeCompare`, so both existing callers keep their exact output.
- `slugFor` is genuinely safe, not just safe-looking: no separator on either platform survives it, no leading `..`, and the mandatory `-<deck>` suffix rules out Windows reserved device names as a side effect.
- `buildFor` is a pure-ish function returning bytes as well as a path, so the Open key test can assert on the URL and the package test on the layout without either reaching a real disk.
- The `fromOffer` docblock and the report both record the warp-classification gap rather than papering over it.

### Issues

**Critical** — none.

**Important**

1. `streamdeck/.gitignore` does not cover the new runtime output. It already carries `*.sdPlugin/bin` and `*.sdPlugin/logs`, which exist precisely because `npm run watch` links the repo's `.sdPlugin` folder into the Stream Deck app and the SDK writes into it at `cwd()`. `buildFor` writes to the same base, so a dev session that follows a run of an unshipped pack leaves `streamdeck/com.scrthq.runlog.sdPlugin/profiles/on-demand/<packid>-<deck>.streamDeckProfile` untracked in the repo, named after the pack id. Given the private-pack boundary, a stray `git add -A` is a plausible way for that id to land in a commit. One line fixes it: `*.sdPlugin/profiles/on-demand` beside the other two. (CI packs from a clean checkout, so the release artifact is not at risk.)

**Minor**

2. `offered.add(packId)` happens before the device loop (`plugin.ts:86`), so if `streamDeck.devices` is empty or holds only Pedals at that moment, the pack is marked as offered and never built for the rest of the plugin run — a deck plugged in later gets nothing. The pre-existing `switchedFor` gate has the same shape, so this is consistent rather than new, but the two flags now guard different things.
3. `buildFor` does not check `hasKeys`. A run whose pack publishes no moves, counters or resources still writes a file and raises an import prompt for what amounts to the generic layout plus a Rules key. The brief scoped the null cases to "no snapshot, no device layout", so this is in spec; the package already exports `hasKeys` and the web page uses it to decide whether to offer a download at all, so the two surfaces now differ on that question.
4. The adapter equivalence holds only where `commands == setups`. A warp that `fitsTheWire` rejects appears in `setups` but not `commands`, so `fromOffer` gives it an Apply setup key while `fromPack` would give it a Command key. This is arguably the correct answer (the page offers no Command for it either), but it is a second divergence beside the documented op-only-warp one and is neither commented nor tested.
5. Nothing ties `ui/open.html`'s option list to the `OpenTarget` union, so a seventh target could be added in one place and not the other. Pre-existing gap, not introduced here.
6. `install` is called once per device on first attach, so a two-deck desk gets two import prompts at once — the accepted ruling, noted here only because the guide copy says "the Stream Deck app asks whether to import it", singular, and a two-deck streamer will see two.

### Assessment

**Task quality: Approved**

The commit does what the brief asked and the parts that were most likely to go wrong are the parts held down hardest: the 44 committed zips rebuild byte for byte, the two adapters are tested against each other rather than against a golden file, the slug sanitizer survives every traversal shape I threw at it, and the plugin-dir resolution matches the SDK's own `join(cwd(), "logs")` line rather than guessing. Every command in the brief runs clean, the manifest is untouched, the docs name no packs and carry no em dashes, and the commit subject and trailer-free body are exact. The one thing worth fixing before merge is the missing `.gitignore` entry for `profiles/on-demand`, which is a one-line change with a real private-pack leak path behind it; the rest are notes for the next pass rather than blockers.
